body_text: Release Details Talphera Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update Aug 12, 2026 PDF Version NEPHRO CRRT clinical study of nafamostat is 75% enrolled; expected to be complete this year Draft 2026 KDIGO guidelines added nafamostat as an acceptable CRRT anticoagulant, a positive change from previous guidelines Updated market research indicates an estimated 200,000 annual U.S. CRRT procedures, a 21% increase over prior estimates; investor event planned as enrollment nears completion Cash and investments of $17.1 million at June 30, 2026 Conference call and webcast to be held on Wednesday August 12, 2026 at 4:30 pm ET SAN MATEO, Calif. , Aug. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Talphera, Inc. (Nasdaq: TLPH), ("Talphera"), a specialty pharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative therapies for use in medically supervised settings, today announced financial results for the second quarter of 2026 and provided a corporate update on the development of nafamostat. "Reaching 75% enrollment in the NEPHRO CRRT study keeps us on track for completion by year-end," stated Vince Angotti, CEO of Talphera. "Site realignment is complete, with all target clinical sites now activated. We are particularly pleased with the high level of engagement from our principal investigators and study site personnel." "In addition, the evolving treatment landscape continues to reinforce the potential role for nafamostat in CRRT. The KDIGO 2026 Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) and Acute Kidney Disease (AKD) is currently pending final publication following the close of its public comment period in May. The guideline references nafamostat as an acceptable regional anticoagulant during CRRT. This is a positive change from KDIGO's last published AKI guidelines," continued Mr. Angotti. "Separately, our updated market research on CRRT treatment patterns indicates that approximately 200,000 CRRT procedures will be performed in 2027 in the U.S., an increase of 21% over our prior estimate. As we near completion of enrollment, we look forward to hosting an investor event to share these findings and discuss the commercial opportunity for nafamostat, if approved, including the potential favorable implications of the evolving KDIGO guidelines." Second Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights 75% enrollment in the NEPHRO CRRT clinical study which is expected to be completed this year. Completed our clinical site realignment, with all target clinical sites now activated. KDIGO published its 2026 guideline and completed a public comment period, citing nafamostat as an acceptable CRRT anticoagulation alternative, a positive change from the last published recommendations. KDIGO (Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes) is the global non-profit organization developing and implementing evidence-based clinical practice guidelines in kidney disease. Completed updated market research indicating approximately 200,000 annual U.S. CRRT procedures in 2027, a 21% increase over prior estimates. Regained Nasdaq compliance with the $1 bid price rule. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Information The cash and investments balance was $17.1 million as of June 30, 2026. Combined R&D and SG&A expenses for the second quarter of 2026 totaled $3.9 million compared to $3.7 million for the second quarter of 2025. Excluding non-cash stock-based compensation expense, these amounts were $3.7 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to $3.5 million for the second quarter of 2025. The increase in combined R&D and SG&A expenses in the second quarter of 2026 was primarily due to higher Niyad development expenses, reflecting increased enrollment. Net loss attributable to common shareholders for the second quarter of 2026 was $4.3 million, or $0.06 per basic and diluted share, compared to a net loss of $3.5 million, or $0.10 per basic and diluted share, for the second quarter of 2025. Conference Call and Webcast Talphera will hold a conference call and webcast at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time/1:30 p.m. Pacific Time today to discuss the results and provide an update on the Company's business. Conference Call and Webcast Information Date: Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 4:30 PM ET/1:30 PM PT Participant Dial-in (North America): 1-800-836-8184 Participant Dial-in (International): 1-646-357-8785 Conference ID: 50873 Webcast Access: Click here The event can also be accessed in the Upcoming Events page in the Investors section of the Talphera website at www.talphera.com . A replay of the webcast will be available on the Talphera website for 90 days after the event. About Talphera, Inc. Talphera, Inc. is a specialty pharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative therapies for use in medically supervised settings. Talphera's lead product candidate, Niyad® is a lyophilized formulation of nafamostat and is currently being studied under an investigational device exemption (IDE) as an anticoagulant for the extracorporeal circuit, and has received Breakthrough Device Designation status from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This release is intended for investors only. For additional information about Talphera, please visit www.talphera.com . About Niyad and Nafamostat Nafamostat is a broad spectrum, synthetic serine protease inhibitor with anticoagulant, anti-inflammatory and potential anti-viral activities. Niyad® is a lyophilized formulation of nafamostat and is currently being studied under an IDE, as an anticoagulant for the extracorporeal circuit, and has received Breakthrough Device Designation Status from the FDA. Talphera's registrational study of Niyad is named the NEPHRO CRRT ( N afamostat E fficacy in Ph ase 3 R egistrational C ontinuous R enal R eplacement T herapy) study. An ICD-10 procedural code, XY0YX37, has been issued for the extracorporeal introduction of nafamostat. The ICD-10 code is a specific/billable code that can be used to indicate a procedure. LTX-608 is a proprietary nafamostat formulation for direct IV infusion that may be investigated and developed for the treatment of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), acute pancreatitis or as an anti-viral treatment, amongst other potential targets. About the NEPHRO CRRT Study The NEPHRO CRRT Study is designed as a prospective, double-blinded trial to be conducted at up to 14 U.S. hospital intensive care units. The study will enroll and evaluate 70 adult patients undergoing renal replacement therapy, who cannot tolerate heparin or are at risk for bleeding. The primary endpoint of the study is mean post-filter activated clotting time using Niyad versus placebo over the first 24 hours. Key secondary endpoints include the mean post-filter activated clotting time over 72 hours, filter lifespan, number of filter changes over 72 hours, number of transfusions over 72 hours and dialysis efficacy (based on urea concentration) over the first 24 hours. title: Huracanes y El Niño: la combinación que pone en jaque a la logística mundial
summary: El Niño no solo altera el clima: también paraliza puertos, cierra rutas y encarece fletes. Descubre cómo este fenómeno afecta las cadenas de suministro.

Huracanes y El Niño: la combinación que pone en jaque a la logística mundial Puertos saturados, rutas bloqueadas y sobrecostos a la vista: así es como el binomio climático más comentado del año puede reescribir el mapa del comercio global Conocimiento Industria 13/08/2026 Cada temporada, cuando los organismos meteorológicos anuncian el regreso de El Niño, la conversación pública gira casi siempre alrededor del clima: más calor, más lluvia, más sequía. Pero detrás de esos titulares hay una historia menos visible y mucho más costosa para las empresas: la de las cadenas de suministro que dependen de que un puerto opere sin interrupciones, de que un canal tenga suficiente calado o de que una carretera siga transitable después de una tormenta. El Niño no genera huracanes por sí solo, pero sí modifica las condiciones atmosféricas y oceánicas que determinan dónde y con qué fuerza se forman los ciclones tropicales. Esa alteración, sumada a los cambios de temperatura y precipitación que el fenómeno provoca en distintas regiones, expone a la logística internacional a interrupciones que van mucho más allá de un mal pronóstico del tiempo. ¿Cómo afectan los huracanes a la logística? Un huracán no solo representa un riesgo mientras toca tierra. Su impacto en las cadenas de suministro comienza días antes, cuando navieras y operadores portuarios deben decidir si desvían embarcaciones, retrasan salidas o cierran terminales de manera preventiva, y se extiende mucho después de que la tormenta se disipa. Durante episodios de El Niño, la actividad ciclónica no desaparece: se redistribuye. En el Pacífico oriental suelen intensificarse las condiciones favorables para la formación de huracanes, mientras en otras cuencas oceánicas el comportamiento puede ser distinto. Para las empresas, ese reacomodo geográfico significa que rutas consideradas “seguras” en un año normal pueden dejar de serlo, obligando a replantear itinerarios con poco margen de anticipación. Los efectos operativos son concretos. Un puerto que suspende maniobras por vientos superiores a cierto umbral detiene simultáneamente la carga, la descarga y el tránsito de decenas de embarcaciones. Las terminales de contenedores acumulan inventario que no puede moverse, generando cuellos de botella que tardan días (a veces semanas) en desahogarse una vez restablecida la operación. A eso se suman los daños directos: grúas dañadas, accesos inundados y personal que no puede trasladarse a sus centros de trabajo. El transporte terrestre tampoco queda exento. Carreteras cerradas por deslaves, puentes comprometidos y vías férreas inundadas pueden aislar zonas productivas completas, incluso cuando el huracán ya se alejó. El verdadero costo logístico de un ciclón rara vez se mide en las horas que dura la tormenta, sino en las semanas que toma reconstruir la conectividad entre fábricas, almacenes y puntos de venta. Para las compañías que operan cadenas de frío o manejan mercancías sensibles al tiempo, el riesgo se multiplica: cada hora de retraso puede traducirse en pérdida de producto o clientes insatisfechos. Por eso, cada vez más empresas incorporan el monitoreo de ciclones tropicales a sus protocolos de continuidad operativa, no como un evento excepcional, sino como una variable recurrente de planeación. Logística internacional: cuando el problema de otros se vuelve propio La segunda cara de este fenómeno es su alcance global. Las cadenas de suministro modernas están diseñadas para ser eficientes, no necesariamente para ser resistentes, lo que significa que una disrupción localizada puede propagarse rápidamente a través de una red de proveedores, transportistas y fabricantes interconectados en distintos continentes. Un ejemplo reciente ilustra esta dinámica. Entre 2023 y 2024, la sequía asociada a El Niño redujo los niveles de los lagos que alimentan el Canal de Panamá, obligando a restringir el número de tránsitos diarios y el calado permitido. La medida tuvo repercusiones que llegaron mucho más allá de Centroamérica: navieras que conectan Asia con la costa este de Estados Unidos y con América Latina enfrentaron mayores tiempos de espera, rutas alternativas más costosas y un incremento generalizado en las tarifas de flete. Ese caso demuestra algo que las empresas latinoamericanas no siempre dimensionan: no es necesario que un huracán toque las costas de la región para sentir su impacto. Si un ciclón afecta un puerto asiático clave o interrumpe la navegación en un corredor marítimo estratégico, las consecuencias se transmiten en mayores tiempos de tránsito, alzas en las tarifas de transporte y retrasos en la llegada de insumos. Lo mismo aplica a componentes electrónicos, materias primas y productos manufacturados cuya fabricación se concentra en zonas vulnerables a fenómenos climáticos extremos. Esa dependencia geográfica, sumada a la creciente frecuencia de eventos disruptivos, ha llevado a que diversificar rutas y proveedores deje de ser una estrategia opcional para convertirse en un requisito de supervivencia operativa. Prepararse antes de que llegue la tormenta La lección de los episodios recientes de El Niño es clara: la resiliencia logística ya no puede construirse solo con la experiencia histórica de una región. Requiere monitoreo constante de pronósticos hidrometeorológicos, alertas tempranas sobre ciclones tropicales, rutas alternativas previamente identificadas y una visión que abarque no solo la operación local, sino los eslabones internacionales de los que depende cada cadena de suministro. Relacionado Maria Saucedo María es una periodista experimentada que combina su formación en letras con una visión estratégica de la logística, creando contenido inspirador e informativo para nuestro blog. title: RingCentral call recording: How it works, its limits, & what to know
summary: Find out how RingCentral call recording works, which plans include it, and the key storage and retention limitations you should know before committing.
body_text: Looking for a business phone that offers phone call recording? With RingCentral, you’ll get access to call recording in all of its plans. On-demand recording is available on every plan, and automatic recording is available on the Advanced plan and higher. But there’s a catch you should know: recording storage retention. On the Core and Advanced plans, recordings are kept for only 90 days before they’re permanently deleted. Even in its most expensive tier, this data retention period applies. If you’re a business that needs permanent access to your call recordings, you should look for a different business phone provider. In this article, we explain how RingCentral’s call recording features work and how they fall short for most businesses. We’ll also share a RingCentral alternative you should consider so you can build better relationships with your customers. RingCentral call recording at a glance Curious about RingCentral’s call recording features and how they’re distributed across its plans? Here’s an overview of its features in RingEx, its business phone offering: RingCentral uses real-time AI call transcription so that you can review what was discussed right after a call ends. Check out our deep dive into RingCentral AI tools . For a full breakdown of what each tier costs and includes, see our RingCentral pricing guide. How to record calls in RingCentral Setting up call recording in RingCentral takes a few steps in your phone number settings. You can set them up the same way whether you have on-demand or automatic call recording. Here’s how: Sign in to the Admin Portal . Click the Phone System tab. In the left panel, click Company Call Handling . Under Call recording , turn on the toggles for either On-demand call recording or Automatic call recording . Keep in mind that in many US states, you’re legally required to inform the other party that a call is being recorded. RingCentral lets you configure an automatic announcement, but you’ll need to enable it manually in the Admin Portal. Once recording is enabled, the real question becomes how long you can access those recordings and how much storage you actually get. How to access, listen to, and download RingCentral call recordings You can access call recordings in RingCentral’s desktop and web apps, the mobile app, and in the admin portal. Here’s how: RingCentral desktop & web app In the navigation bar, click Phone . Click the Recordings tab, then select a recording. The details will appear in the main panel. For any recording, you have these options: View . View the caller’s name and phone number, with options to call, fax, text, or message the caller. You can also add the caller to your contacts list or block their number. Play . Click the Play icon to listen to the recording. Use the slider to fast-forward or rewind. Download . Click the Download icon to save the recording as an MP3 file. RingCentral mobile app In the bottom toolbar, tap Phone . Tap the Recordings tab. Tap any recording to view the details and access the controls. For any recording, you have these options: View. View the caller’s name and phone number, with options to call, text, send a message, or view their profile. Play. Play or stop the recording. Speaker. Switch the audio source to speaker. Copy. Tap and hold their name to copy the phone number. Share. Send the recording to another person. RingCentral admin portal Sign in to the Admin Portal . If it shows Admin Portal at the top right, click the dropdown, then click My Extension . Click the Messages tab. In the left panel, click Recordings. Choose what you want to do with a call recording: Play. Click the Play button to listen to any recorded call. Use the slider to fast-forward or rewind. Download. Click the three-dot More icon, then select Download . Forward. To send the recording through email, click the three-dot More icon, then select Forward . 🚨 Note: RingCentral doesn’t have a bulk export feature to download all your recordings. You’ll have to download each recording individually if you want to be able to access them longer than 90 days. RingCentral call recording limitations Here are the biggest limitations of RingCentral’s call recording features: 1. 90-day call recording retention If you can’t store call recordings in your business phone, should you record them at all? With RingCentral, you risk losing your recordings 90 days after you record them. Even if you upgrade to its Ultra plan, you can’t change this 90-day limit. If you have long sales cycles or need to resolve a customer dispute six months down the road, you won’t have access to valuable context in your recordings. RingCentral recommends you download your recordings so you have access to them, but there are two challenges with this approach. No conversation context. You don’t have the context you need in your business phone workspace. Recordings are downloaded with some metadata, but you lose context about the texts and calls you had before and after a specific recording. No bulk export. You have to download your recordings individually from your RingCentral account. You can’t export recordings in bulk, which adds another task for your team. It isn’t enough to export your recordings either. You have to store, organize, and label them so your team can actually use them. 2. Recording volume caps RingCentral doesn’t just delete recordings after 90 days; it limits how many recordings you can store in your account. Automatic call recordings are capped at 100,000 per account. On-demand recordings are capped at 200 per user. For high-volume departments in sales and support, these limits can affect your team’s usage over time. Team members may skip recording calls to save workspace storage. Your CRM hygiene will be affected, which can affect your sales performance metrics too. 3. Recording announcement friction To stay compliant with call recording laws in different US states, RingCentral offers call recording announcements in its platform. However, these announcements are intrusive when talking to your customers. You can play a voice message to notify callers that the call is being recorded. But the only other option is a periodic audio tone, which means that callers will constantly be reminded the call is being recorded. Call recording limitations are just one piece of the picture. For a full breakdown of RingCentral pros and cons, see our RingCentral review . RingCentral call recording vs Quo: A breakdown Call recording is an essential feature for managing your customer relationships and improving your team performance. But RingCentral might hold you back. Here’s a comparison of RingCentral’s call recording features with Quo, formerly OpenPhone. Quo is a modern business communications platform that gives you access to essential call recording features without limiting your usage. Here’s where Quo call recordings have an edge over RingCentral: No storage limits. Quo lets you store as many call recordings as you need in our platform. You have access to your recordings as long as you maintain an active account. Share recordings with other tools. With our third-party integrations, you can share your recordings wherever your team works. Our CRM integrations sync recordings with call logs in your Salesforce and HubSpot accounts. Compare this with RingCentral integrations. Flexible call recording announcements. Quo offers voice- and audio tone-based call recording announcements. You can upload a custom audio file to notify callers that their call is being recorded. Don’t just take our word for it. Businesses have rated Quo the #1 business phone by customer satisfaction on G2. Here’s a Quo customer reviewing our call recording features: “It’s fantastic. With call recordings and transcripts, we can just say, ‘Tell me where you live and what’s your email address.’ Then it records it all for us to refer to later.” – Brett Colquitt, Owner, OC Tasker Want to see where else we excel compared to RingCentral? See the full side-by-side comparison in our Quo vs RingCentral breakdown. FAQs Where are RingCentral call recordings stored? Call recordings are stored in RingCentral’s servers and are accessible in the admin portal and RingCentral apps. Recordings can be downloaded for local storage, but there’s no bulk export tool. Automatic recordings are capped at 100,000 per account, and on-demand recordings are limited to 200 per user. When should you consider RingCentral call recording alternatives? Here’s a quick checklist to help you answer whether you should go with a RingCentral alternative for your call recording needs: • If you need to access recordings after three months for training or compliance purposes. • If your call volume is growing rapidly and you don’t want to worry about recording storage in your business phone. • If you want more flexible call recording announcements. Why is my RingCentral call recording not working? Here are a few things you can do to make sure your RingCentral workspace is recording calls: • Verify your plan supports the recording type you want. • Confirm call recording is enabled in the Admin Portal for the right site and numbers. • Check that each user has permission to record calls. If older recordings are missing, remember they’re deleted after 90 days. If problems persist, contact RingCentral support. Is RingCentral call recording legal? Whether you can legally record a call depends on your state and the other party’s location, not on RingCentral. Some US states require only one-party consent; others require two-party consent. RingCentral lets you record and configure a recording announcement, but compliance is your responsibility. Confirm the consent laws that apply to you before recording. How does RingCentral call recording compare to other alternatives? RingCentral’s call recording limitations aren’t shared by alternatives like Zoom Phone or Nextiva. See our full breakdown of RingCentral vs Nextiva .

title: XBiotech Scientists Demonstrate Therapeutic Potential of IL-1α Blockade in Pulmonary Melanoma
summary: XBiotech is conducting a Phase I study to evaluate the safety and pharmacokinetics of its stroke therapy candidate, Hutrukin, in healthy volunteers.
body_text: A new study published in Scientific Reports by scientists at XBiotech highlights the promise of targeting interleukin-1 alpha (IL-1α) to combat metastatic melanoma. Using Flo1-2a—a murine surrogate for XBiotech’s anti-IL-1α monoclonal antibody vilamakitug (Natrunix, XB2001)—researchers demonstrated that neutralizing IL-1α markedly suppressed pulmonary tumor nodule burden and significantly prolonged survival in preclinical mouse models. The therapy effectively disrupted key metastatic and immunosuppressive drivers, downregulating crucial genes and proteins including MMP2, MMP9, VEGF, and PD-L1. These findings support IL-1α blockade as a powerful therapeutic approach for treating advanced, metastatic melanoma. ‍ 🔗 Read the full study: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-66972-6

title: Pre-Med Volunteer Opportunities in San Diego
summary: This guide covers where pre-med students can volunteer around San Diego, how to apply, and what to expect once you start.
body_text: Volunteering is an essential part of the pre-med experience. Medical school admissions committees want to know you have been out in the world seeing how healthcare affects real people, not just holed up in the library studying. They know that interacting with patients and healthcare teams will give you empathy and build the communication skills that will make you a better doctor. The bonus is that it gives you material for your personal statement and letter-of-recommendation opportunities that go beyond grades and test scores. San Diego is a great place to find hands-on, pre-med volunteer experiences . The city and greater county are home to major health systems, a VA hospital, a dedicated children's hospital, and a wide network of community clinics serving diverse patient populations. Finding the right opportunity here isn't always simple, though. Popular hospital programs can have waitlists, strict age or hour requirements, or application windows that only open once or twice a year. This guide is designed to help. It covers where to volunteer around San Diego, how to apply, and what to expect once you start. We’ll also talk about a paid role that can complement your volunteer work and strengthen your med school application. Volunteer Opportunities for Pre-Med Students in San Diego San Diego's pre-med volunteer opportunities generally fall into four categories: hospitals and health systems, hospice, community clinics and nonprofits, and academic and research. Each builds a different kind of experience, and the strongest applications usually combine more than one. Here's where to start looking around San Diego: San Diego Hospital and Health System Volunteer Programs San Diego's major hospital systems all run structured volunteer programs. Most require an application, interview, and health clearance before you can start, so factor in an on-ramp period when considering your timeline. UC San Diego Health Roles: Volunteers support patients and staff in helping with wayfinding, errands, stocking, deliveries, and visiting with patients. Requirements: Applicants must be at least 16 and commit to a weekly four-hour shift for a minimum total of 100 hours over six to eight months. You must provide immunization/vaccination records, a TB test, and a background check. Application process: Onboarding takes about a month. You must complete an online training course, attend an in-person orientation, and do any other training required by the department where you will volunteer. Sharp HealthCare Roles: Sharp places volunteers across its San Diego hospitals in roles like visitor greeting, patient companionship, and gift shop support. Requirements: Each hospital has its own requirements, which you can find on their site. They have minimum age and GPA requirements for students, as well as a minimum time commitment. Application process: The process includes an interview, orientation, and health screenings, which they will specify during onboarding. Scripps Health Roles: Scripps volunteers help with tasks ranging from welcoming guests to cleaning and clerical support. They even have special programs related to canine therapy, crafts, and music. Requirements: Applicants must be at least 15 years old and commit to two to four hours a week for a minimum of six months or 100 hours. Application process: Onboarding takes several weeks and includes an interview, a mandatory orientation, and immunization requirements. Kaiser Permanente San Diego Roles: Volunteers may work at hospitals, medical offices, or hospice locations. Support includes wayfinding, visiting with patients, deliveries, pet therapy, arts, and other support for patients and families. Requirements: Applicants must be 16 or older and commit to a three- to four-hour shift per week. Volunteers over 18 must commit to 120 total hours of service and pass a health clearance and background check. Application process: Training sessions and onboarding requirements vary by location and role. Rady Children's Hospital Roles: Support is needed in a variety of settings, including inpatient, outpatient, and emergency departments. Requirements: Applicants must be 18 or older and commit to one weekly three-hour shift for a minimum of 100 hours over 12 consecutive months. You must pass certain health screenings, a drug screening, and a background check. There are also required vaccinations. Application process: Rady's application process isn't always open, so it's worth checking the page regularly for the next window. VA San Diego Healthcare System Roles: Clinical opportunities include supporting staff in nursing, pharmacy, speech, and radiology. You may also support patients and families as an ambassador or greeter in surgical waiting rooms. Requirements: Volunteers may work at a community-based clinic or the main hospital. Requirements vary by location and role. Some require health screenings and a background check. Application process: Applications are accessed online by linking to a specific facility. Volunteer program requirements, application cycles, and minimum hours at these hospitals change often, so confirm current details directly on each site before you apply. Learn about Stepful's 5-Month Online Medical Assistant Program Explore Program San Diego Hospice Volunteer Programs Hospice work gives pre-med students a different kind of exposure than a hospital floor, one centered on companionship, comfort, and end-of-life care. It's one of the highest-impact volunteer categories for medical school applications. Hospice Volunteering with VITAS Healthcare Roles: Volunteers can fill administrative or patient-facing roles, like one-on-one visits with patients and their families in their homes or at hospice facilities. The site lists many opportunities, including Direct Patient Care. Requirements: Volunteers who are 18 or older can join the interdisciplinary team and are eligible for many different roles. Other requirements may include health screenings, depending on the role and location. Application process: Complete a volunteer application, attend an orientation session, and complete VITAS's free volunteer training. Sharp HospiceCare Roles: Nonmedical support for patients and families, including caregiver relief, companionship, light housekeeping, and help with outings and errands. There are also administrative and clerical roles. Requirements: Applicants must commit to at least four hours a week for one year, provide a CA driver's license and proof of auto insurance, two letters of recommendation, and a $25 registration fee ($10 for students). There are also required health clearances. Volunteers 18 and older also must undergo a background check. Application process: Submit the application by email or mail, complete an interview, then attend the three required training sessions. The Elizabeth Hospice Roles: Volunteer patient companions provide caregiver relief, social visits, light housekeeping, and run errands. There are also other roles available. Requirements: Applicants must commit for at least one year. Hours are scheduled around a patient’s needs, but a typical weekly shift is four hours or less. Training is provided. Application process: Call or email to sign up for a volunteer orientation, where you'll learn about the application and training process. San Diego Community Clinics and Nonprofit Health Organizations Community clinics and nonprofits can offer more direct exposure to underserved patient populations than a large hospital. Some roles may be administrative or event-related, but some may provide even closer contact with patients than a typical hospital volunteer shift. Family Health Centers of San Diego Roles: General volunteer positions support health education, patient engagement, and clerical work in FHCSD's clinics. There are also a limited number of student internships each year. Requirements: Applicants must be at least 18, commit to a minimum of 100 total hours, and complete a background check and health screening, including TB testing and proof of COVID-19 vaccination. Application process: Apply online, attend an information session, and complete a department interview. After finishing the 100-hour minimum, FHCSD can provide a letter documenting your role and hours for med school applications. Volunteers in Medicine (VIM) San Diego Roles: Volunteer front desk managers support the clinic by checking in patients, answering the phone, assisting doctors and nurses, scheduling, and more. Requirements: Not listed publicly; VIM reviews applications and follows up directly about current openings. Application process: Submit the online volunteer application. VIM will reach out with details on available positions. UC San Diego Student-Run Free Clinic Project Roles: Undergraduate volunteers help patients access low-cost or free medication, support patient intake, manage inventory and supply ordering, collect and enter patient data, and more. They work alongside medical student volunteers and supervising physicians. Requirements: Requirements vary by role and will be posted with open positions. Application process: Announcements about open positions and application procedures are posted in their Facebook group . Mama's Kitchen Roles: Volunteers deliver medically tailored meals or prep food in the kitchen for San Diegans living with HIV/AIDS, cancer, and other chronic illnesses. Requirements: Delivery drivers must complete a background check and use their own vehicles. Weekly commitments are encouraged. Kitchen volunteers have no specific requirements and can sign up for shifts on an online schedule. Application process: Complete a volunteer registration form and a virtual orientation. San Diego Blood Bank Roles: Volunteer bloodmobile greeters greet and support donors, make them feel at ease, help them fill out intake forms, and answer their questions. Requirements: Applicants must be 15 or older. Shifts run four to six hours. Application process: Submit a volunteer application and attend an orientation before your first shift. American Red Cross , Southern California Region Roles: Volunteers support work like disaster relief response and blood drives. Requirements: Background checks are required for all adult volunteers, but other requirements vary by role. Time commitments are also variable. Application process: Complete an online application and submit a background check, then a volunteer screener will contact you with next steps. Organizations may change their roles, requirements, or application cycles, so confirm this information before applying. San Diego Research and Academic Volunteer Opportunities Unpaid research roles at San Diego's universities and medical schools build a different kind of experience, one that MD/PhD and research-focused MD programs value. There are a few ways to find these positions. The most common is direct outreach to the faculty member running the research project. However, some scholar programs and individual research projects may also have online applications. University pre-health advising offices are a good source of curated, regularly updated listings, even for students not enrolled at that school. The University of San Diego's pre-health resources page , for example, lists many local options. Here are a few specific opportunities you can explore. UC San Diego Emergency Medicine Research Associates Program Roles: Students screen, enroll, and interview emergency department patients for clinical research studies under faculty and resident supervision. Requirements: Applicants must first become Health System Volunteers through UC San Diego Health Volunteer Services . You must commit to at least 100 hours in six months and show proof of health screenings and a background check. Then, you must complete a variety of training requirements depending on the role and location. Application process: The program accepts applications only at certain times of year and then reviews them on a rolling basis. Check the site to find out when applications are being accepted. San Diego State University Department of Psychology Research Labs Roles: Students volunteer as unpaid research assistants in faculty labs studying a variety of factors related to human behavior. They help with data collection, literature review, and other ongoing lab work. Requirements: Students must be in good academic standing. The site recommends getting involved as early as possible in your academic program. Application process: Students identify a lab of interest, then contact the principal investigator directly by email or during office hours to ask about openings. Some labs require a formal application, which you can download. How to Find and Apply for Pre-Med Volunteer Opportunities Once you know which kind of opportunities interest you, the actual search-and-apply process looks pretty similar across most San Diego organizations. Search the sites of organizations directly. Don’t rely on an aggregator or third-party volunteer site. Organizations also list the most up-to-date requirements. Here’s a list of categories to get you started: The volunteer pages on hospital and health system websites Websites of community clinics and nonprofits Hospice websites Pre-health advising offices at universities Pre-med clubs and organizations, like AMSA chapters or Alpha Epsilon Delta ‍ Websites for volunteers like Idealist Submit an application and prepare for an interview with a volunteer coordinator. Complete any required health clearances, immunizations, and background checks. Requirements vary by organization and change over time, so confirm exactly what's needed for each volunteer role. Keep in mind that they may need to be done before you submit your application. Attend orientation and any required training. Start volunteering and track your hours. Review what medical schools want to know about your experience and keep a log of those items. That will make filling out your AMCAS application and prepping for interviews much easier later on. Learn about Stepful's 5-Month Online Medical Assistant Program Explore Program What to Expect When Volunteering: Best Practices for Pre-Med Students Volunteering rarely looks like the medical dramas that got you interested in the field in the first place. Going in with realistic expectations helps you get more out of the experience and avoid burning out. Here are some tips that may help: Expect administrative or indirect tasks at first. Remember that even roles like greeting patients or restocking supplies put you in a clinical environment and teach you how care teams actually function. Keep a short journal or notes after each shift. Specific moments, not general impressions, are what make personal statements and interview answers memorable. Ask questions and build relationships with staff and physicians when appropriate (not in front of patients). These connections can turn into a letter of recommendation down the road. Show up reliably and follow through on your commitment. Consistency matters more to admissions committees than raw hours. Reflect on what you learn about yourself. Given how competitive medical school admissions have become, being able to explain specifically why an experience confirmed your interest in medicine matters as much as the experience itself. Balancing Volunteering with Academics and MCAT Prep Volunteering matters, but not at the expense of your GPA or MCAT score. Those numbers carry more weight in the admissions process than the volunteer hours themselves. Here are some tips for keeping things in balance: Don’t commit to more than you can handle. Most organizations ask for one shift a week of a few hours. Being consistent with that commitment counts more than just piling on hours. Communicate with your volunteer coordinator when you have exams or tougher class loads. Most coordinators will let you pause or scale back if you just let them know your needs. Avoid signing up for more than you can reasonably sustain. A shorter list of consistent commitments looks stronger on an application than a long list of one-time events. Consider Becoming a Medical Assistant to Strengthen Your Med School Application Medical schools want pre-med students to get clinical experience so they can learn what working in healthcare is really like. Volunteering in a clinic gives you exposure and shows a willingness to serve, but paid clinical work takes your experience a step further. Medical assistants work alongside clinicians and interact with patients. Working as a medical assistant can help you get into med school , but it can also help you confirm that this is a career you really want before you commit years to a medical degree. Medical assistants do both clinical and administrative tasks, mostly in outpatient settings like doctors' offices. They take vital signs, perform basic lab tests, prepare patients for exams, and assist physicians during visits. They also schedule appointments and manage medical records. You can become a certified medical assistant in a matter of months by following this path: Step 1: Enroll in a training program. Stepful's medical assistant program is a good example of an online program that is flexible enough for pre-med students. Live classes happen twice a week online, and you get an at-home clinical kit to practice hands-on skills. The program takes 5 months to complete. Step 2: Get certified. Your training program should prepare you to pass a national certification exam . Certification isn't required in every state, but most employers prefer or require it. Step 3: Complete a clinical externship. Programs like Stepful's offer an 80-to 160-hour in-person externship at a real clinical site. This lets you graduate with real patient-care experience, not just classroom instruction. Step 4: Apply for MA jobs. Once certified, you can look for part-time or full-time roles at clinics, hospitals, or urgent care centers in our area. Programs like Stepful’s provide one-on-one career coaching, resume and interview prep, and job search support. Medical assistants have a unique opportunity to learn from physicians on every shift. It’s also a great way to develop relationships with physicians that can lead to strong letters of recommendation for your med school application. Learn about Stepful's 5-Month Online Medical Assistant Program Explore Program Pre-Med Volunteering in San Diego FAQs How many volunteer hours do medical schools expect from applicants? The general consensus is that somewhere between 150 and 300 volunteer hours is the right amount. Doing more doesn’t make your application better. What matters most is consistent, meaningful involvement rather than hitting a specific number. Do I need to volunteer at a hospital specifically, or do other settings count? Other settings count. Community clinics, hospice organizations, and research labs all give admissions committees a fuller picture of your interest in medicine and your willingness to serve others. How early should I start volunteering as a pre-med student? Starting during your first or second year of college gives you time to build meaningful, long-term commitments instead of scrambling to log hours right before you apply. Consistency over multiple years matters more than an early start alone. Can shadowing count as volunteering? No. AMCAS tracks shadowing and volunteering as separate categories, since shadowing involves observing rather than actively helping. Most applicants include both. You can learn more about shadowing a doctor here . Do ride-alongs with fire departments or EMS count as volunteer hours? Not usually. A typical ride-along, where you observe without performing hands-on duties, falls under AMCAS's shadowing category rather than volunteering. It's still worth doing and worth including on your application, but it would be logged separately from your volunteer hours. Is paid clinical work like being a medical assistant a substitute for volunteering? It's not a substitute, but it strengthens your application. Admissions committees generally value paid clinical roles as strong evidence of hands-on patient care experience. Most applicants benefit from having both paid work and volunteer service on their application. What if a hospital's volunteer program is closed to new applicants? Don't wait around for one program to reopen. Community clinics, research labs, and hospice organizations often have more flexible timelines. Applying to a few different types of programs improves your odds of getting started sooner. How does volunteering affect my overall chances of getting into medical school? Volunteering alone won't get you into med school , but its absence can hurt you. Combined with strong grades, a competitive MCAT score, and clinical experience, it rounds out the profile admissions committees look for.

title: You'll never measure every building. You can still plan like you have.
summary: Get the full value of the space data you already have. Portable Profiles lets one measured building sharpen decisions across your portfolio.
body_text: Real estate and workplace teams are making multi-million-dollar decisions right now about spaces they haven't measured. Whether to grow or consolidate, whether a floor can absorb a new team, whether to renew a lease: these are some of the most expensive and hard-to-reverse calls your team makes, and you are making them in buildings where you have never had measurement to tell you whether the decision will actually work the way you are betting it will. The truth is that you are never going to measure every square foot of your portfolio. So the decision about Building A gets made on gut feel and rough proxies, even though Building B right down the road is measured, and the people in it work similarly to those you're planning for. So what if you could take everything you already know about how your people use space in Building B, and use it to plan Building A? That's why VergeSense created Portable Profiles. We take how your people actually use your space in a measured building and turn it into a profile you can carry into a plan for another building. Now that office you never measured is planned around how your own people really behave. You right-size it, reconfigure it, or plan its capacity with a forecast grounded in your company and context. With Portable Profiles, you finally get the full value of the measurement you already paid for. One measured building stops being a single data point and starts sharpening decisions across your entire portfolio. You get to plan confidently everywhere, without having to wire up everything to get there. If that sounds obvious, it's worth asking why no one has done it before, and that’s because the design of a space changes how people behave inside it. Give people more conference rooms, for example, and they tend to hold more meetings. So you cannot simply copy "how Building B was used" onto Building A, because you would be carrying over Building B's walls, not how your people behave. To build a profile that actually travels, we had to separate the two: the unique way your employees work from the behavior the building itself was inducing. Pulling those two apart is only possible if you have seen enough workplaces to know which is which. That is what VergeSense’s Large Spatial Model does. It’s trained on more than 250 million square feet of real workplace behavior, the largest behavioral dataset in the industry, and it is what lets us tell your people's patterns apart from the patterns their building imposes on them. Portable Profiles is live for VergeSense customers today. If it is something you want to put to work across your portfolio, talk to your CSM now.

title: Sales contract management 101: How to get deals signed faster
summary: A practical guide to sales contract management: the 5-stage lifecycle, what breaks + the tools and practices that get contracts signed in days, not weeks.
body_text: Sales contract management is the process of taking a deal from "verbal yes" to a signed agreement: drafting, negotiating, approving, signing, and tracking it after the fact. Sounds simple, but it rarely is. Most B2B teams lose deals here because the contract gets stuck. Legal's backed up. The approval never got routed. Nobody's sure which version is current. The average business loses close to 9% of contract value a year to problems like these. This guide breaks down: What sales contract management is, and how it's different from CLM The 5-stage contract lifecycle The biggest failure points revenue teams run into 10 best practices to speed up contracting without adding risk What to look for in contract management software Let's get into it. 👉 Get Started with GetAccept's Contract Management Software for Free What is sales contract management? Sales contract management is the process of creating, negotiating, approving, signing, storing, and tracking sales agreements across the deal cycle. It covers everything from the moment a deal is ready to move to paper (or screen) through to signature and beyond. That includes drafting the initial agreement, managing redlines and negotiations, routing for internal approvals, getting the buyer to sign, and tracking what was agreed after the ink is dry. Sales contract management vs. CLM vs. general contract management These three terms overlap, but they solve different problems at different speeds. General contract management covers the full spectrum of agreements an organization handles: vendor contracts, employment agreements, procurement deals, NDAs, partnership agreements, and more. It's broad, and it's typically owned by legal or procurement. CLM (contract lifecycle management) is the system layer. It's the infrastructure for managing any contract from creation through to renewal or termination: templates, version control, approval workflows, obligation tracking, e-signature. CLM is category-agnostic. It doesn't care whether the contract is a sales deal or a vendor agreement. Sales contract management is the sales-specific operating model that runs on top of CLM. It's built for revenue workflows: CRM-connected intake, commercial terms, sales-led approvals, buyer engagement tracking. The whole system is optimized for speed and commercial accuracy, not just legal completeness. Deals have close dates. Reps have quotas. Buyers have competing priorities. The practical difference : you can have CLM without it being built for sales (and many organizations do, which is why their sales teams hate using it). A well-designed sales contract management process uses CLM capabilities as its engine but wraps them in a workflow designed around how deals move. Deal velocity takes a direct hit. Every day a contract sits unsigned is a day the deal could fall apart. Budgets get frozen. Champions leave. Competitors re-enter. Time kills deals , and slow contract workflows hand time to every force working against you. A sales lead at a public sector procurement software company described proposals taking 40 to 60 minutes each across Excel, Word, the ERP, and SharePoint, and during a busy quarter running around 20 opportunities, having to drop the ball on the deals that didn't fit. Forecasting accuracy falls apart. When contract status isn't visible in your CRM, managers are forecasting based on rep optimism rather than actual deal progress. You can't tell the difference between "legal is reviewing" and "the buyer ghosted us three days ago." That uncertainty compounds up the chain, from frontline managers to the VP of Sales to the CFO, and turns your forecast into guesswork. "Poor forecast accuracy is hurt by the limited deal visibility and understanding of what's actually being reviewed, and how close you really are to closing." — Account management lead, energy technology company Revenue leaks through the cracks. Poor contract management costs money after signature too. The leakage comes from missed renewals, unenforced pricing terms, unauthorized discounts that make it into contracts without approval, and obligations nobody tracks after the ink is dry. Buyer experience suffers. A clunky, slow contract process is a bad first impression of what it's like to work with your company. It also removes your ability to respond. Several teams we spoke with had no way of knowing whether a prospect had even opened a sent proposal, which means follow-up becomes guesswork at exactly the moment the deal is most fragile. Legal becomes an unintentional bottleneck. When every contract, regardless of size or risk, requires a full legal review, the queue builds fast. Without pre-approved templates, clause libraries, and defined fallback positions, legal's time gets consumed by routine deals that don't actually need their attention. That leaves high-value, high-risk agreements waiting longer than they should. The sales contract lifecycle: from opportunity to signed agreement A sales contract lifecycle includes five core stages: intake and pre-authoring, authoring and negotiation, review and approval, execution, and post-execution management. Each stage has distinct owners, handoffs, and failure points. Stage 1: Intake and pre-authoring This is where the contract request originates. A rep has reached verbal agreement with a buyer and needs to generate a contract. The intake stage captures the deal details (pricing, terms, product scope, parties involved) and routes them into the contract creation process. In a well-run system, this happens through a structured intake form or CRM-triggered workflow, not a Slack message to legal. The goal is to capture everything needed to draft the contract accurately the first time. Missing information at intake creates rework later. Stage 2: Authoring and negotiation Once the deal details are captured, the contract gets drafted. In most modern sales environments, this means pulling from a pre-approved template library rather than starting from scratch. The rep, or an automated system, populates the template with deal-specific data. Then comes negotiation. The buyer reviews, requests changes, and the back-and-forth begins. This is where version control, redlining tools, and clear fallback positions matter most. Without them, you end up with conflicting edits, lost changes, and deals that stall because nobody's sure which version is current. Stage 3: Review and approval Before the contract goes to the buyer, or is finalized after negotiation, it needs internal sign-off. Depending on the deal size and complexity, that might mean a manager approval, a legal review, a finance check on pricing, or all three. Sales, legal, finance, and operations should each have defined responsibilities and service-level expectations so routine contracts don't stall waiting for informal handoffs. When approval routing is manual and informal, this stage becomes a black hole where deals disappear for days. Stage 4: Execution This is the signature stage. Both parties sign, ideally through a secure e-signature workflow, and the contract becomes legally binding. In a modern sales process, this should be fast, frictionless, and trackable. Buyers should be able to sign from any device without creating an account or downloading software. Reps should get notified the second the contract is signed. The signed document should sync back to the CRM automatically. Stage 5: Post-execution management The deal is signed, but the contract's job isn't over. After signature, contract management should continue with centralized storage, obligation tracking, milestone monitoring, and renewal or termination management. This is where most teams drop the ball. The signed PDF gets filed somewhere, the rep moves on to the next deal, and nobody tracks what was actually agreed, until a renewal comes up or a dispute arises. Who owns what Ownership varies by company, but a typical breakdown looks like this: Sales owns intake, initial drafting, and buyer communication Legal owns template approval, non-standard term review, and risk assessment Finance or deal desk owns pricing validation and discount approval RevOps owns process design, system integration, and reporting Customer success owns post-signature obligation tracking and renewal preparation When these handoffs are clear and automated, the process moves. When they're informal and manual, deals stall. Common types of sales contracts Contract Type Description Typical Use Case Master Service Agreement (MSA) Framework agreement governing the overall relationship Enterprise relationships with multiple transactions Order form Commercial document capturing pricing, product, and term Specific transactions under an MSA Statement of Work (SOW) Detailed deliverables, timelines, and responsibilities Project-based engagements NDA Non-disclosure agreement Early-stage conversations before detailed info sharing Subscription agreement Terms of ongoing software access SaaS deals The specific mix varies by deal type, company size, and industry. Enterprise SaaS deals look different from professional services agreements. But the core elements are consistent. The biggest challenges in sales contract management Most B2B teams know their contract process is broken. They're less sure exactly where. To find out, we went through our recorded conversations with revenue, finance, and transformation leaders across various industries. Five problems came up again and again: Contracts live everywhere, so they live nowhere The most repeated pain point by a wide margin. Signed agreements end up spread across inboxes, SharePoint, the CRM, ERP systems, local drives and whatever tool the last team used. "Storage is fragmented today. Signed contracts sit in SAP, or in HubSpot, or in a Drive, or on someone's local computer. When a person leaves, a lot of knowledge disappears with them." — Revenue leader, enterprise payments group. The problem compounds with volume. One transformation lead at a fintech described the scale of the lookup problem directly: "So actually locating the correct terms is a bit of a challenge, because there could be 100, 150, 200, 300 order forms associated with that one client." Approval and legal review stall deals for weeks Every non-standard term routes to a human, and those humans have day jobs. What should be a two-day review becomes two weeks because the queue is manual, the reviewers are senior, and nobody can see where a contract is sitting. "I'm currently managing six parallel enterprise deals, and this is 40% of my time — telling the tech team and external and the lawyers to review some clauses. It even goes out of my scope." — CFO, AI sales technology company (early-stage) [verify size] At an employee benefits platform, contract back-and-forth consumed 20-30% of one legal associate's time. And at a large payments group, the gap between a customer saying yes and a signed contract ranged from two to twelve months , with the longest cycles driven by extensive redlining across multiple document versions. Negotiation happens in email and Word, so version control collapses The moment a contract leaves the platform to get redlined, the audit trail fragments. Teams end up reconciling tracked changes across attachments, chat threads, and copy-pasted tables. At a maritime software company, an acquisition took the standard agreement from 4 pages to 42, and the review cycles grew accordingly: "Complex contract management process, increased from 4 to 42 pages after acquisition. Time-consuming legal review with customers. Inefficient back-and-forth about contract terms." — Director of Maritime Sales, maritime training and software company The pattern is consistent: the more the negotiation moves outside a shared system, the more time is spent reconstructing what was agreed rather than agreeing it. Nobody can see renewals, key terms, or contract data Once a contract is signed, the data inside it goes dark. Renewal dates, notice periods, payment terms and risk clauses are locked inside PDFs that nobody has time to read. So renewals get missed, invoices don't match contracts, and risk clauses go undetected. Many teams reported the same pattern from the cost side: missed termination dates on supplier agreements driving avoidable spend, no dashboard view of upcoming renewals, and contract data that employees fill in inconsistently, making the records that do exist unreliable. Manual contract creation produces errors, and errors produce rework Every field a human types is a field a human can get wrong. And in contracting, small errors are expensive because they restart the process. "They wrote on the contract that payments were due 80 days, and that's not what it means. It forced three more interactions in the process because we needed to send a request for change of the contract. It took another week and a half to close something that was already closed." — CFO, AI sales technology company The same CFO described a redlining error where a rep needed to replace "Europe" with "Sweden" three times in a single paragraph and changed it once. And a recurring mismatch where payment data entered manually (wrong ID, wrong tax ID) meant the invoice didn't match the contract. Use pre-approved templates and clause libraries Well-built contract templates reduce repetitive tasks and copy-paste errors. They also protect your brand and help new reps ramp faster by giving them a proven foundation to work from. A typical template must include: A client-facing contract name, set with merge tags so every document is named consistently without manual edits Standard terms and conditions approved by legal Consistent pricing and product sections Optional modules for add-ons or configuration differences Variable fields for company details, dates, and contract specifics A personalization block for messaging that speaks directly to the buyer The goal is simple: build it once, then reuse it confidently across every deal. Establish and automate fallback positions One of the most reliable ways to cut the back-and-forth in contract negotiations is deciding your fallback positions before the negotiation starts, not during it. Not every point needs to go back to legal. Define the terms you're willing to accept without escalation, and build them into your contract workflow. When a buyer pushes back on a standard clause, the rep or deal desk can offer the pre-approved alternative without waiting for a legal review. This alone can cut days off negotiation cycles. Common fallback positions include liability caps (you'll accept 12 months of fees instead of 24), payment terms (net 45 instead of net 30), and auto-renewal language (90-day notice instead of 60). title: FDA approves Pluvicto for PSMA+ metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), advancing potential new standard of care across metastatic disease
body_text: Pluvicto now approved across PSMA+ metastatic prostate cancer, nearly doubling eligible patient population PSMAddition updated results show Pluvicto reduced risk of progression or death by 33% in combination with standard of care (ADT + ARPI) vs. SoC alone, with positive overall survival trend (HR=0.80) mHSPC is incurable and about half of men progress within 20 months, highlighting need for differentiated, precision approaches earlier in disease journey With five US RLT manufacturing sites operational or under construction, Novartis has scale and infrastructure to meet growing demand Basel, July 31, 2026 – Novartis today announced the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Pluvicto® (lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan) in combination with an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) for patients with prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-positive metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naive/sensitive (mAPMN/S) prostate cancer, commonly known as metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC). Approval is based on the Phase III PSMAddition trial, which showed Pluvicto reduced the risk of progression or death by 28% (HR 0.72; 95% CI: 0.58–0.90) when combined with standard of care (SoC; ARPI + androgen deprivation therapy [ADT]) compared to SoC alone. At a subsequent updated analysis, the Pluvicto combination further reduced the risk of progression or death by 33% (HR 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55–0.82) with a positive overall survival (OS) trend favoring Pluvicto plus SoC (HR=0.80; 95% CI: 0.63–1.01), as data continue to mature ahead of final OS analysis. “The treatment landscape for mHSPC is evolving, and this approval reflects a growing recognition that earlier treatment intensification matters,” said Michael Morris, MD, Prostate Cancer Section Head, GU Oncology, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, and a Principal Investigator of the study in the US. “Having a radioligand therapy available at this stage meaningfully expands the options for physicians and represents real progress for patients.” Pluvicto can now be used across all stages of PSMA-positive metastatic prostate cancer, nearly doubling the eligible patient population. The approval builds on its established use in metastatic androgen pathway modulation-resistant (mAPMR) prostate cancer, also known as metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). More than 186,000 men are diagnosed each year with mHSPC globally*1. Despite significant treatment advancements, about a third of patients do not achieve undetectable PSA with ARPI-ADT doublet therapy alone and half will progress to castration-resistant disease within 20 months, highlighting the need for earlier treatment intensification in this disease state2-6. The PSMA biomarker is present in more than 80% of patients with prostate cancer7-11. "This approval signals a new era in the treatment of prostate cancer, representing a shift toward more targeted, early intervention," said Gina Carithers, CEO and President of the Prostate Cancer Foundation. "This milestone redefines prostate cancer care, ensuring that from day one of their metastatic diagnosis, men have a precision option." The safety profile and tolerability of Pluvicto were consistent with its established profile in PSMAfore and VISION. At primary analysis, grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) were reported in 50.7% of patients who received Pluvicto plus SoC compared to 43.0% receiving SoC alone. The most common all-grade AEs were dry mouth, fatigue, nausea, hot flush and anemia. Health-related quality of life was maintained based on longitudinal assessment reflecting patient experience over time, with similar outcomes across arms in PSMAddition. "Pluvicto is now approved across PSMA-positive metastatic prostate cancer, nearly doubling the number of patients who may benefit from this targeted approach," said Victor Bultó, President, US, Novartis. "Patients with metastatic prostate cancer continue to face significant unmet need, underscoring the importance of introducing precision options earlier in the treatment journey. Backed by nearly a decade of leadership in radioligand therapy and continued investment in science and infrastructure, we are expanding this field and bringing its promise to more patients." Novartis RLT Patient and Office Support With five manufacturing sites now operational or under construction in the US, Novartis has established an industry-leading footprint to support its goal of establishing RLT as a fundamental pillar of oncology care. Backed by an integrated end-to-end RLT ecosystem, Novartis can deliver Pluvicto to US treatment sites within 5 days to ensure prompt treatment initiation. Novartis Patient Support is available to help eligible patients get started on treatment, including help understanding insurance coverage and identifying potential financial assistance options. Patients or providers can speak to a live agent at 1-844-638-7222 or visit https://us.pluvicto.com/support/novartis- patient-support . About Pluvicto™ (lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan) Pluvicto is an intravenous radioligand therapy (RLT) combining a targeting compound (a ligand) with a therapeutic radionuclide (a radioactive particle, in this case lutetium-177). After administration into the bloodstream, Pluvicto binds to target cells, including prostate cancer cells that express PSMA, a transmembrane protein. Once bound, energy emissions from the radioisotope damage the target cells and nearby cells, disrupting their ability to replicate and/or triggering cell death. Pluvicto is the only PSMA-targeted agent approved across metastatic prostate cancer. Novartis is also investigating Pluvicto in oligometastatic prostate cancer (PSMA-DC, NCT05939414). Radioligand Therapy (RLT) at Novartis Novartis is reimagining cancer care with RLT for patients with advanced cancers. By harnessing the power of targeted radiation, RLT is designed to deliver treatment directly to target cells anywhere in the body. As a global leader in this space, Novartis has built integrated capabilities across research, manufacturing, logistics, and patient and provider support to help ensure approved RLTs reach patients reliably and efficiently. Novartis is investigating a broad portfolio of isotopes, ligands, and combination therapies to expand the use of RLT beyond prostate and neuroendocrine tumors. title: Channels
summary: Diebold Nixdorf's Branch Design & Deployment team ensures that every branch transformation project we support has access to dedicated branch experts. See examples in our blog.
body_text: When you’re planning branch renovations or de novo branches, the details that make credit unions and banks so unique can get lost or muddled by architects and designers who don’t solely focus on financial institution design. Diebold Nixdorf’s Branch Design & Deployment team ensures that every branch transformation project we support has access to dedicated branch experts. Collaboration is Key For example, at SSB Community Bank, the DN team worked collaboratively with the architect and the bank president, from the site study and pre-construction phase to the ribbon cutting of their new branch. We filled a couple of very specific, critical roles during the process: because we know our products better than anyone, and we work almost exclusively on FI projects, we developed both the initial site drawings and the conceptual building plans. Of course, changes and tweaks were incorporated as we listened to the vision of multiple stakeholders. This enabled us to provide the architect with files of the desired facility design and significantly reduce the timeframe to produce the architectural drawing set. Fixing an Issue Before it becomes a Major Obstacle We see curb widths that restrict reach, designs that don’t accommodate service-technician access to self-service terminals, VAT tube runs that are rerouted to avoid obstructions, misplaced products and several other issues that can cause aggravations and expensive work-arounds when they’re eventually uncovered. We’re all about the details, and these issues can be eliminated when the DN Branch Design & Deployment team is engaged early in an opportunity. The Power of Renderings Our clients are usually surprised to see their branch concepts come to life. The 3D renderings allow key decision makers to fully understand the project before construction begins. Plus, once we’ve completed renderings, our clients are free to use them as marketing materials, by repurposing them on an easel in their current lobby, on a billboard or even on social media. Modern Design for the Way Branches Operate Today Let’s face it, the retail branch continues to evolve, and it’s tempting to quickly adopt emerging technologies. However, this strategy doesn’t guarantee success unless properly implemented to fit business goals. We believe technology should complement building lasting relationships with customers, and not be a distraction. Our holistic design approach balances technology and services placement in any environment, allowing staff to leverage each customer engagement to its fullest potential. Talk with your Diebold Nixdorf rep about how the Branch Design & Deployment team can support your own branch design, renovation or new-build efforts .

title: Redwire and Kanematsu Announce Strategic Collaboration to Drive Innovation and Deliver Next-Generation Space Solutions for Japan’s Space Sector
summary: Tokyo, Japan (August 12, 2026)- Redwire Corporation (NYSE: RDW), a global leader in aerospace and defense technology solutions, announced that it has signed a teaming agreement with Kanematsu…
body_text: Tokyo, Japan (August 12, 2026 )- Redwire Corporation (NYSE: RDW), a global leader in aerospace and defense technology solutions, announced that it has signed a teaming agreement with Kanematsu Corporation (hereinafter “Kanematsu”). The collaboration combines Redwire’s advanced space technologies with Kanematsu’s extensive market expertise to support the growth of Japan’s space industry. Under the terms of the agreement, Kanematsu will serve as Redwire’s strategic commercial partner in Japan, supporting business development across both private and public sector space infrastructure offerings and related products, including power generation systems, microgravity payloads, and robotics technology. “Through our partnership with Kanematsu, we look forward to working alongside Japanese industry to advance innovative space technologies to further bolster Japanese capabilities for a wide variety of commercial, scientific, and national security applications,” said Mike Gold, President of Redwire Space. “Space-based capabilities impact nearly every aspect of industrial capacity and Redwire looks forward to collaborating with Kanematsu to create innovations in fields as diverse as pharmaceuticals, biotech, power generation, and Earth observation. We’re proud to be partnered with Kanematsu, an extraordinary and trailblazing organization, to show how work in space can benefit life on Earth.” “We are thrilled to partner with Redwire, a proven leader in cutting-edge space infrastructure,” said Ryoichi Kidokoro, COO, Motor Vehicles & Aerospace of Kanematsu Corporation. “As Japan’s space ecosystem enters a dynamic new era of growth, integrating Redwire’s world-class technologies—from advanced robotics to microgravity payloads—with Kanematsu’s deep market expertise and commercial network will unlock incredible value. Together, we are committed to driving innovation and delivering next-generation space solutions to both public and private customers in Japan.” The teaming agreement was signed on July 8, 2026, at Kanematsu Headquarters during the annual SPACETIDE event in Japan. About Redwire Redwire Corporation (NYSE:RDW) is an integrated aerospace and defense company focused on advanced technologies. We are building the future of aerospace infrastructure, autonomous systems, and multi-domain operations leveraging digital engineering and AI automation. Redwire’s approximately 1,400 employees located throughout North America and Europe are committed to delivering innovative space and airborne platforms transforming the future of multi-domain operations. For more information, please visit RDW.com. Media Contact: Tere Riley [email protected] OR Investors: [email protected]

title: 5 Wildly Different Trucks Reveal the Scope of Mopar’s Direct Connection Catalog
summary: It’s only appropriate that Brian Szalk, the man in charge of Ram’s factory-backed parts catalog, is restoring—and modifying—one of the earliest muscle trucks.
