title: Security National Financial Corporation Reports Financial Results For The Quarter Ended June 30, 2026
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Security National Financial Corporation's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: PDF Version SALT LAKE CITY, Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Security National Financial Corporation (SNFC) (NASDAQ symbol "SNFCA") announced financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. For the three months ended June 30, 2026, SNFC’s after-tax earnings increased 7.3% from $8,371,000 in 2025, to $8,982,000 in 2026. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, after-tax earnings increased 8.1% to $15,983,000, from $14,784,000 in 2025. Scott M. Quist, President of the Company, said: “I am pleased to report that our second quarter earnings, after tax, increased 7.3% over 2025, and that our first-half earnings increased 8.1%, after tax, over 2025. This improved profitability for both the quarter and the first half of the year illustrates the very solid operational and sales progress we have made in all of our business segments. It is not lost on me that our top-line revenue decreased 6.3% for the quarter and 5% for the half. We are working aggressively, and in my view successfully, to address those revenue issues. But our first goal was improved profitability, and we achieved that goal. Our Mortgage Segment can be considered the “star” for the first half of 2026, delivering two very solid quarters of improved performance. The Mortgage Segment improved Q1 year-over-year profitability by $1.4MM and then followed that great performance in Q2 with a $1.6MM improvement, for a total $3.0MM profit improvement for the first half of 2026. Revenue did decrease 9.1% for the first half, which is never our goal, but that decrease highlights the tremendous operational improvements that were accomplished. Obviously, there is a nexus between revenue and profitability, but in this market if we must choose one or the other, meaning revenue growth or improved profitability, at this juncture I much prefer the improved profitability. A “shout out” is owed to the entire company for this improved performance. Suffice it to say that all aspects have been worked, worked again, and reworked over the last several years, including management structures, margins, marketing, commissions, products, pricing, back office, secondary operations, underwriting, and closing and funding, to achieve greater efficiencies. Much work remains to be done, but after all the hard work of our team it is gratifying to see this Segment profitable in Q2 and within striking distance of profitability for the year. Our Cemetery and Mortuary Segment also delivered stellar results increasing revenue by 21% for the quarter and by 13% for the first half, with a corresponding profit improvement of 69% for the quarter and 29% for the first half. As is many times the case, there is much movement going on “under the hood” in achieving those impressive results. First, the overall backdrop. While it is difficult to precisely quantify at this time, I believe most would agree that the death rate in the United States dropped in 2026 to its lowest level in recent years. The improved mortality experienced in our Life Insurance Segment, decreased case counts in our funeral funding operations, and reviews of our publicly-traded peers all reinforce that conclusion. Thus, looking within this Segment at our mortuary-only results, while revenue did increase by some 3% for the first half, profitability actually decreased some 9%. We believe that we have generally increased our market share, but it has been a struggle because of this year’s declining death rate. However, demonstrating the benefit of diversified income streams, our cemetery-only results showed an 11% revenue improvement with a 17% profitability improvement, basically as the result of improved preneed cemetery sales. Our cemetery preneed sales results show that we are controlling that which we can control, which is leading to overall profit improvement. Many thanks to the considerable effort that has gone into rebuilding our preneed cemetery sales force. In addition to the improved preneed sales results, we had a $1MM favorable investment tailwind in the second quarter, which reversed the unfavorable investment results we experienced in the first quarter. All in, we achieved a nearly 23% Segment net profit margin in the first half, which in my view is admirable. Our Life Insurance Segment also made very significant positive progress despite its top-line revenue decrease of 5.5% for the first half and a profitability decrease of 13%. I don’t believe those numbers are illustrative of the significant progress which has been accomplished in nearly all facets of our business. Regarding the revenue decrease there are two major components, which are premium revenue, the smaller component of the decrease, and investment income revenue. While there are numerous inputs into the reported premium amount, which makes generalizing somewhat hazardous, to me the premium revenue decline is primarily due to fewer single-premium products being sold in 2026, which in my view is our least profitable product. Our modal-pay product sales have actually increased year-to-date, but those effects won’t be realized in our financial statements for several periods. As I have noted in prior releases, we have been spending significant time and resources in improving our sales functions, which efforts in my view have been very successful even being measured at this very initial stage. Illustrative of that initial success, first-year premium sales are now up vs. 2025. We have much work to do, but we have built, and are building, excellent offerings for the marketplace, to include a much improved onboarding process for new sales personnel, ease of application for both the agent and the customer, quicker real time underwriting decisions, better lead generation and management, more predictable commission and advance structures, and better quality measuring metrics, all resulting in significant first-year traction. The larger factor in this Segment’s revenue decline, and probably also the larger factor in its profitability decline, is its investment income. Specifically, we had lower builder profit splits in 2026 vis a vis 2025, and also decreased interest income. We have made specific strategic decisions to increase our landholdings, which in my view will lead to greater profits in the future, albeit at the cost of current profitability since we recognize no profit on land until it is either sold or a home on it has started construction. Many of our landholdings have a 12 to 24 month, or longer, time horizon, so increasing landholdings does suppress both revenue and profit in the current period, in favor of greater profitability in the future. Regarding the decrease in interest income, this result reflects the impact of loan payoffs, increased rate competition, and lower loan origination volumes during Q1. Construction-related loan originations, however, rebounded strongly during Q2. Utah new-home starts were down significantly in 2025 (which trend appears to be continuing in 2026), which led to decreased construction loans. Primarily due to lower loan production our cash position has increased by some $61MM since Dec 31, 2025, which does earn “bank interest” but at a rate below that of our lending activities. Despite those declines, I don’t believe we have ever had better processes or more talented and capable people in responsible positions than we do today. In summary, I believe we have improved capacity, more talented people, greater wherewithal, and better sales offerings in both product and processes, than we have ever had. In a nutshell, when viewed as a whole, SNFC increased profitability in the quarter by 7.3%, and for the first half by 8.1%, despite a decline in revenue. Many thanks to our hard-working teams for achieving those impressive operational results.” SNFC has three business segments. Is Muzz Safe? What We Actually Do About Catfish, Scammers and Harassment
summary: Learn how Muzz combats catfish, scammers, fake profiles and harassment with selfie verification, moderation and privacy features.
body_text: Muzz requires every member to complete selfie verification before they can be seen. Profiles are manually reviewed, blocking and reporting are free and available to everyone, and photo privacy is on by default rather than sold as an upgrade. Muzz has over 10 million members and 800,000 success stories. Looking for your soulmate? You won’t find your soulmate on this blog post but you might find them on Muzz - the world’s biggest Muslim dating and marriage app. Sign Up muzz It’s a fair question, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a paragraph about how much we value your trust. So here is what Muzz actually does, what it doesn’t do, and what you should do yourself – on Muzz or anywhere else. Is Muzz a legitimate app? Muzz is a Muslim marriage app founded in 2015 by our co-founder Shahzad Younas, who left a career at Morgan Stanley, taught himself to code and built the first version of the app himself. It went through Y Combinator, reached its first million users in 2016, and rebranded from Muzmatch to Muzz in 2022. Today Muzz has over 10 million members and more than 800,000 success stories – couples who met on the app and got married. Muzz is independently owned. It has never been sold to a larger dating (Zionist) conglomerate, and its founder has stated publicly and repeatedly that it will not be. Free Palestine forever and always. Does Muzz verify every profile? Yes. Selfie verification is mandatory on Muzz, not an optional badge and not a paid feature. Every member submits a selfie, which is compared against their profile photo to confirm the profile belongs to a real person. That selfie is never shared with anyone – not with other members, not with third parties – and is used only for security. Muzz also reviews profiles manually. Photos that don’t meet the guidelines are rejected, and every member has to show their face in their verification selfie. Manual review is slower than pure automation, and that’s deliberate. Muzz also monitors behaviour, not just profiles. Accounts that like or message at volume – fast, indiscriminate, the pattern of someone working through a list rather than looking for a spouse – get flagged automatically and reviewed by a person. Muzz founder Shahzad Younas has written publicly about how the company approaches this, and he’s blunt about it: it’s a permanent cat-and-mouse game, and he won’t claim it’s solved. (ref: https://x.com/ShahzadYounas_/status/1889686271515058626?s=20 ) Some context from that thread worth repeating: Scammers target relationship apps specifically, because people there are emotionally open and are often too embarrassed to report being defrauded. These aren’t opportunists – Muzz has encountered organized operations running scams as full-time work from dedicated offices. What Muzz uses against them: device identification, selfie and facial-similarity recognition, and further methods the company deliberately doesn’t publish. A significant focus is stopping blocked scammers from simply signing up again – the single measure that most affects whether a removal actually sticks. Muzz tracks how long a suspected scammer exists on the platform before being detected and removed, and that window has narrowed meaningfully as these measures have come in. The goal is removal before the account can match or message anyone at all. Shahzad has also noted the uncomfortable part: AI now makes some deception nearly impossible to spot by eye, which means increasingly using AI to detect AI. Honorable mention: Only women review verification selfies. Muzz’s community team is all women, by design. For sisters who wear hijab or niqab, or who simply don’t want their face reviewed by a man, verification shouldn’t mean a trade-off — so it isn’t one. The selfie you submit is seen by a woman on the Muzz team, and by no one else. It never appears on your profile, is never shown to other members, and is never shared outside Muzz. Are there fake profiles and catfish on Muzz? Any platform with millions of members attracts people acting in bad faith. Pretending otherwise would be the least trustworthy thing an app could do. What Muzz does about it: mandatory selfie verification at signup, manual profile review, and an investigation process for impersonation reports. If you think someone is impersonating another person, report them and Muzz will investigate. How to spot a fake profile One photo, or several that look like the same shot. Real profiles have variety – different settings, different lighting, different days. A bio with nothing specific in it. Generic virtues and no details about their actual life is a signal. They refuse a video call. Muzz has free in-app video calling. Someone serious about marriage will use it. Someone who won’t, after weeks of chatting, is telling you something. They want to move off the app immediately. Wanting your snapchat or WhatsApp within the first few messages usually means they want to be somewhere with no verification, no moderation and no reporting. The story escalates fast. Intense declarations early, then a crisis, then a request. That’s the shape of a romance scam. Money enters the conversation at all. An emergency, an investment opportunity, a visa problem, a gift card. No exceptions, no matter how good the reason sounds. How do you block or report someone on Muzz? Blocking is free, takes seconds, and works two ways. From their profile: open the profile, scroll to the bottom, select Block, choose a reason, submit. From your chat: open the chat, tap the three dots in the top right, and under Safety Options select Block, then confirm. Two things worth knowing, both documented publicly by Muzz: They are not notified. The person you block is never told. It works both ways. They can’t see or message you, and you won’t see them either. Reporting is separate from blocking, and you should do both when someone’s behaviour breaks the rules rather than just being a bad match. Reports go to the moderation team for review, and Muzz operates a ban appeals process so decisions can be contested. What safety resources does Muzz offer? Muzz runs a Safety Center at muzz.com/us/en/safety/ with four sets of published guidelines: Profile Quality Guidelines – what makes a thoughtful, halal profile Behavior guidelines – the standard Muzz expects of members and what breaks it Safety Guidelines – practical advice for using the app safely Safety Resources – external helplines, including Samaritans, Women’s Aid, and Muslim counselling and Muslim women’s support services The Safety Center also carries emergency contact guidance. If you feel unsafe right now, call 911 first. Report to Muzz afterwards. How does Muzz protect your privacy? Photo privacy is standard on Muzz, not a paid upgrade. Members who prefer to keep their photos hidden for privacy or modesty can do that on the free tier. Muzz also offers free in-app voice and video calling, so you can see and speak to someone before meeting them without exchanging phone numbers. If you’d like to exchange phone numbers but we believe it is too early, we’ll actually nudge you by asking “Are you sure you want to share personal information?” One point of confusion worth clearing up: the Gold feature relating to blurred photos is a filter that lets paying members hide profiles whose photos are blurred. It does not change anyone’s ability to protect their own photos. Hiding yours is free. Why does Muzz limit you to five conversations? Muzz caps active conversations at five. Once you have five going, browsing pauses until you unmatch someone. You can have unlimited matches – the limit is on conversations, not connections. This has been documented in the Muzz help center since the feature launched, and the reason is straightforward: five real conversations that go somewhere are worth more than fifty that don’t. The limit applies to everyone, including Gold members. It isn’t a paywall and there is no version of Muzz you can buy that removes it. Muzz also prompts you when a conversation goes quiet from either side, to check whether you want to keep talking. What Muzz is doing about ghosting Relationship apps have a problem, and everyone using one already knows what it is. You send a message. Nothing. You send another. Seen, two weeks ago. Eventually you stop asking. Ghosting isn’t a safety issue in the way harassment or scams are. Nobody is in danger. But on an app built for marriage, being left hanging with no answer is its own kind of disrespect, and it is the single most common complaint we hear. So Muzz built accountability into the mechanic. If you have unanswered conversations, browsing stops until you deal with them – reply, or unmatch. Both are valid. Walking away is allowed. Disappearing while someone waits is not. Ending a conversation respectfully is a feature, not a failure. Not every match is the one, and saying so is kinder than silence. Is Muzz free, and what does Gold change? Matching and chatting on Muzz are free, and Muzz has committed to keeping them that way. You do not need to pay to meet someone or to talk to them. Gold adds: must-have filters so you only see matches within your preferences, more daily likes, a free weekly Profile Boost that puts you in front of around 30x more people, a filter to hide blurred-photo profiles, a hideable VIP badge, and Rematch after an unmatch. What Gold does not do: remove the five-conversation limit, unlock verification, or gate your own photo privacy. Safety features are not on the paid tier. How to stay safe on any Muslim marriage app This applies whether you use Muzz or not. Video call before you meet. The single most effective anti-catfish step there is, and it’s free on Muzz. Stay on the app early. Verification, moderation and reporting only work while you’re on the platform. Never send money. Not for an emergency, not for a flight, not for an investment. There is no version of this that ends well. Meet in public the first time (with a mahram). A café, a restaurant, somewhere with people. Bring someone if you want to. Tell someone where you’re going. A friend, a sibling, a parent — the person’s name, the place, the time. Guard your details. Home address, workplace, financial information — none of it belongs in an early conversation. Trust the feeling. If something is off, you don’t owe anyone an explanation. Unmatch, block, report. Frequently asked questions Is Muzz safe to use? Muzz requires mandatory selfie verification for every member, manually reviews profiles, and offers free blocking and reporting to all users. Photo privacy is available on the free tier. As with any app, your own precautions — video calling before meeting, staying on-platform early, never sending money — matter alongside the platform’s. Does Muzz verify its users? Yes. Every member must complete selfie verification, which compares a submitted selfie against the profile photo to confirm a real person is behind the account. The selfie is never shared with anyone and is used only for security. Verification is not a paid feature. Are there fake profiles on Muzz? Any large platform attracts bad actors. Muzz counters this with mandatory selfie verification, profile review, and an investigation process for impersonation reports. If you suspect someone is impersonating another person, report them. How do I block someone on Muzz? From their profile: scroll to the bottom, select Block, choose a reason, submit. From a chat: tap the three dots, then Block under Safety Options. They are not notified, and the block works both ways — they can’t see or message you, and you won’t see them either. What happens when you report someone on Muzz? Reports go to the moderation team for review, which can result in a ban. Muzz operates an appeals process so banned members can contest a decision. Why can’t I browse when I have five conversations? Muzz caps active conversations at five so members focus on real conversations rather than collecting matches. Reply or unmatch to free a slot. Matches are unlimited – only conversations are capped, and the limit applies to Gold members too. Does Muzz Gold remove the five-conversation limit? No. The limit applies to every member regardless of subscription. Gold adds filters, likes, Profile Boosts, Rematch and a VIP badge — it does not change conversation limits or unlock safety features. Is Muzz free? Yes. Matching and chatting are free and Muzz has committed to keeping them free. Gold is optional and adds visibility and convenience features. Still have a question? The Muzz help center covers profile setup, verification, safety and privacy, and the Safety Center holds the community guidelines and external support resources. If you feel unsafe right now, contact the police first.

title: Amazon EC2 introduces application status checks
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon EC2 introduces application status checks
body_text: Amazon EC2 introduces application status checks, a new status check that helps customers detect and respond to application-level issues on their EC2 instances. With application status checks, EC2 monitors applications to detect issues such as a web server that has stopped accepting requests, a Docker daemon that is not running, an incorrect networking configuration, or a network interface that is no longer passing traffic. Customers rely on EC2 status checks today to receive alerts when an instance or the underlying system is unreachable. However, to monitor application issues, customers had to build and maintain their own monitoring solution. Now, with application status checks customers can monitor the status of their applications running on EC2 instances alongside existing EC2 instance and system status checks. Customers create a check by specifying the protocol, port, and path to monitor, along with the response codes that indicate a healthy application. After customers associate the check with their instances by instance ID or tag, Amazon EC2 sends HTTP or HTTPS requests to that port and path and reports on the application’s status every 60 seconds. Auto Scaling groups act on application status, initiating recovery by replacing instances when their applications report unhealthy. Application status checks are available in all commercial AWS Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To get started with application status checks and review pricing, see the Amazon EC2 User Guide .

title: What Is CloudKit? Apple’s Backend Explained
summary: Learn what CloudKit is, how its private, shared, and public databases work, what it costs, and when it makes sense for your first Apple app as a beginner.
body_text: CloudKit is Apple’s backend as a service for app developers. It lets your app store structured data in iCloud, sync that data across a person’s devices, and share data between users without requiring you to build and operate a traditional server. Imagine you’re building a to-do list app. Someone creates a task on their iPhone, checks it off on their iPad, and later opens the app on their Mac. CloudKit can keep that data synchronized across every device signed into the same iCloud account. CloudKit uses the person’s existing Apple Account for access to private data. Your users don’t need to create another account with an email address and password just to use your app. CloudKit is a compelling option when you’re building a native app for Apple platforms and need cloud storage, syncing, or collaboration. What problem does CloudKit solve? Most apps need somewhere to store their data . You can save data directly on the device, but that data may disappear if the app is deleted or the device is lost. The traditional solution is to build a backend. That usually involves: Running a server Creating a database Building an API Managing user accounts Handling authentication Monitoring security and performance Paying for hosting as the app grows CloudKit handles many of those responsibilities for you. It can store app and user data, synchronize it across devices, share it with other users, and give developers tools for monitoring and managing the database. You still have to design your app’s data model and write the code that uses it, but you don’t need to build an entire backend from scratch. Bitrig has support for CloudKit built right in so it can handle all of this for you, saving you a lot of time. Why would an app developer use CloudKit? CloudKit has several benefits that make it especially attractive to independent developers and small teams. It’s built into Apple’s ecosystem CloudKit is a first-party Apple framework. You don’t need to add a third-party database SDK to your project just to start using it. It integrates with Swift, Xcode, SwiftData, Core Data, and Apple’s signing and capability system. This makes it a natural fit for native apps running on Apple platforms. Users can access private data through iCloud For private and shared data, CloudKit uses the Apple Account that’s already signed into iCloud on the device. Think about the experience of using an app such as Notes. You don’t create a separate Notes username and password. You sign into your Apple Account once, and your information becomes available across your devices. CloudKit lets your app provide a similar experience. Your app still needs to handle situations where someone isn’t signed into iCloud or CloudKit is temporarily unavailable. However, you don’t have to create and secure a completely separate authentication system for basic private-data syncing. You don’t operate the server Apple manages the underlying cloud infrastructure. You don’t have to maintain database servers, install security updates, or wake up because your hosting provider ran out of memory. You can focus more of your time on the app itself. That doesn’t mean CloudKit removes every backend concern. You still need to design your schema, test syncing, handle errors, plan migrations, and monitor the production environment. It simply removes a large amount of infrastructure work. It supports privacy-focused data storage CloudKit provides account-based protection for private and shared data. It also supports encrypted fields for sensitive values stored in private records. Public database records are different. They’re intended for information that may be accessible to everyone using the app, so you should never treat the public database as private storage. Apple explains the available protections in its CloudKit encryption documentation . What are the three CloudKit databases? A CloudKit container separates data into three database types: private, shared, and public. The database you choose depends on who should own the data and who should be able to see it. CloudKit database Who the data belongs to Who can access it Common examples Private One user That user and your app Personal tasks, journal entries, photos Shared Originally one user, then shared The owner and invited participants Shared lists, collaborative notes, shared photo album Public The app or its community Potentially every app user, depending on permissions News, schedules, public posts, shared catalogs Private database Use the private database when data belongs to one person. Examples include: Tasks in a personal to-do app Journal entries Saved favorites Personal documents A person’s custom collections Every user gets their own private database inside your CloudKit container. One user can’t simply browse another user’s private records. The main benefit is syncing. Someone can create data on an iPhone and access the same data from an iPad or Mac signed into the same iCloud account. Private data is stored within the user’s iCloud account rather than consuming your app’s public storage allocation. Shared database Use the shared database when one person wants to share some of their private data with other people. Imagine a grocery-list app. A user creates a private list and then invites their partner to collaborate. The owner still controls the original data, but invited participants can access the shared records according to the permissions your app provides. Other examples include: A shared travel itinerary A shared photo album Household chores Notes shared between coworkers CloudKit provides APIs for creating shares, inviting participants, setting permissions, and removing access. Apple provides a CloudKit sharing sample that demonstrates the underlying concepts. As of August 2026, SwiftData does not support CloudKit sharing. You will need to use Core Data if you intend to use the shared database in your app. Public database Use the public database for information that should be available across your app’s user base. For example, I use CloudKit in a Formula 1 app that displays the same standings and race schedule to every user. That information belongs to the app rather than one specific person, so the public database is the logical place to store it. Other public database examples include: News articles Public events Product catalogs Community posts You can control which users are allowed to create, read, or modify different public record types. However, the public database shouldn’t contain information that needs to remain private. How does CloudKit organize your app’s data? CloudKit uses a few terms that will help you understand how everything fits together. Containers A CloudKit container is the top-level space that holds your app’s databases and configuration. Containers keep one app’s CloudKit data separate from another app’s data. Some developers also use a shared container when multiple related apps need access to the same information. Record types A record type describes a category of data. In a to-do app, you might create record types named: Task List Tag You can think of a record type as being similar to a model type in Swift or a table in a traditional database. Records A record is one individual piece of data. One task called “Buy groceries” would be a record of the Task record type. Another task called “Book hotel” would be a separate record. Fields Fields contain the values stored inside a record. A task record might contain: A title A completion status A due date A priority A reference to its list This is similar to the properties you would define on a Swift model. Relationships and schema Records can be related to other records. A List record, for example, might be connected to several Task records. The complete definition of your record types, fields, indexes, and relationships is called your schema. You can inspect and manage this schema through the CloudKit Console. Apple’s web-based console also provides access to test data, server logs, telemetry, alerts, and production database activity. How do SwiftData and Core Data work with CloudKit? You can communicate with CloudKit directly using the CloudKit framework, but that isn’t your only option. Apple’s local persistence frameworks can also manage much of the synchronization process. SwiftData with CloudKit SwiftData (the successor to Core Data) can automatically synchronize compatible model data through CloudKit when your app has the correct capabilities and configuration. You define your SwiftData models, save them locally, and configure the model container to use CloudKit. SwiftData then manages the persisted store and synchronization. Apple provides a guide to syncing SwiftData model data across a person’s devices. Automatic syncing is convenient, but it isn’t magic. Your schema still needs to be compatible with CloudKit, and you need to test migrations, relationships, deletion behavior, conflicts, and first-time synchronization. As of August 2026, SwiftData does not support CloudKit sharing. You will need to use Core Data if you intend to use the shared database in your app. Core Data with CloudKit Core Data can synchronize a persistent store through NSPersistentCloudKitContainer . This gives established Core Data apps a way to maintain a local copy of their data while mirroring changes through CloudKit. Apple’s Core Data and CloudKit setup guide covers the required capabilities and persistent-container configuration. Direct CloudKit access Using the CloudKit framework directly gives you more control over records, zones, queries, subscriptions, and synchronization behavior. That control also means more code and more responsibility. For many beginner apps, starting with SwiftData or Core Data synchronization may be easier than building a complete CloudKit layer manually. Is CloudKit free? CloudKit is mostly free, but there are a few important details. As of August 2026, CloudKit is included with the paid Apple Developer Program, which costs $99 per year in the United States. You can learn more in our guide to the free and paid Apple developer accounts. Apple currently includes up to 1 petabyte of free public CloudKit storage for each app with the membership. One petabyte is an enormous amount of storage for most independent apps. Private data lives in each user’s iCloud account, so it scales differently from the data in your app’s public database. You shouldn’t interpret this as unlimited free infrastructure for every possible workload. Storage allowances, request limits, transfer limits, and Apple’s program terms can change. Check the current CloudKit information before making major architectural or financial decisions. What are CloudKit’s limitations? CloudKit is powerful, but it isn’t the right backend for every app. It’s designed primarily for the Apple ecosystem CloudKit’s strongest integrations are with native Apple platforms. Apple also provides CloudKit JS for web interfaces and HTTP-based CloudKit web services. Technically, CloudKit isn’t restricted exclusively to native Apple apps. However, there’s no equivalent first-party CloudKit SDK designed specifically for building a full Android app. If your product needs equally important iOS, Android, and web clients from the beginning, a platform-neutral backend may be easier to manage. It depends on iCloud Private and shared CloudKit data depends on the user having an available iCloud account. Your app needs to gracefully handle someone who is signed out, has restricted iCloud access, or temporarily can’t reach the service. You have less infrastructure control Not running a server is one of CloudKit’s biggest benefits, but it can also be a limitation. You don’t control Apple’s infrastructure or every part of the synchronization schedule. Complex server-side processing, specialized search systems, custom authentication flows, and deeply platform-independent APIs may require a different backend or an additional server component. Schema changes require planning Changing a local model during early development is easy. Changing a production cloud schema after real users have stored data requires much more care. Test your data model, migrations, and production deployment process before releasing the app. Should you use CloudKit for your app? CloudKit is worth exploring when most of the following are true: You’re building primarily for Apple platforms. Your app needs to sync data across a user’s devices. You want users to share selected data with other people. You don’t want to operate a traditional backend. An iCloud-based user experience fits your app. Your data can be represented using records, fields, and relationships. You’re comfortable depending on Apple’s ecosystem. Consider another solution when: Android support is a major requirement. You need a platform-neutral authentication system. Your backend requires extensive custom server-side processing. You need complete control over infrastructure and synchronization. Your app relies on specialized database or search capabilities that CloudKit doesn’t provide. CloudKit doesn’t have to handle every part of your app. Some apps use it for private synchronization while relying on another service for public APIs, payments, analytics, or custom processing. How do you get started with CloudKit? At a high level, the process looks like this: Decide whether your data should be private, shared, or public. Join the paid Apple Developer Program if you haven’t already. Add the iCloud and CloudKit capabilities to your Xcode project. Create or select a CloudKit container. Define your model using SwiftData, Core Data, or CloudKit records. Test with multiple devices and Apple Accounts. Inspect the development data and schema in CloudKit Console. Deploy the schema to production before releasing the app. Monitor logs and telemetry after launch. This article is only a high-level introduction. Before shipping a production app, spend time learning about account availability, schema deployment, record zones, error handling, conflict resolution, and data migration. Frequently asked questions Is CloudKit a database? CloudKit is more than a traditional database. It’s a backend service that provides cloud databases, iCloud-based account access, syncing, sharing, subscriptions, monitoring, and development tools. Your data is stored as records containing fields and relationships. Do CloudKit users need to create an account? Users generally don’t need to create a separate email-and-password account for private CloudKit data. CloudKit uses the Apple Account signed into iCloud on their device. Your app still needs to check whether the account is available and explain what happens when iCloud access is disabled. Does CloudKit work offline? CloudKit itself is a cloud service, so network access is required to send and receive server changes. However, SwiftData and Core Data can maintain local persistent data and synchronize it through CloudKit when a connection becomes available. Exact offline behavior depends on how your app’s persistence and syncing are implemented. Can CloudKit sync between an iPhone, iPad, and Mac? Yes. CloudKit is designed to synchronize data across Apple devices that have access to the same user or shared data. Apple currently supports CloudKit across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS, and the web. Can CloudKit share data between users? Yes. One user can share records with other iCloud users and give them permission to view or edit the shared data. Shared lists, collaborative notes, trip planning, and family collections are common examples. As of August 2026, SwiftData does not support CloudKit sharing. You will need to use Core Data if you intend to use the shared database in your app. Is CloudKit a replacement for Firebase? It can replace Firebase for some Apple-first apps, particularly when the main requirements are private iCloud storage, device syncing, and user-to-user sharing. Firebase and similar services may be a better fit when Android support, custom authentication, extensive server logic, or a platform-neutral backend are important. Does CloudKit require the Apple Developer Program? CloudKit is included as an advanced capability with paid Apple Developer Program membership. As of August 2026, the membership costs $99 per year in the United States. The bottom line CloudKit is Apple’s backend service for storing app data in iCloud, syncing it across devices, and sharing it between users. It’s a strong choice when you’re building a native Apple app, want an iCloud-based experience, and don’t want to build and maintain your own server. It’s less compelling when Android support or complete backend control is a major requirement. The easiest next step is to identify what data your app needs to store and decide whether each piece belongs in the private, shared, or public database. Try Bitrig Bitrig helps new developers build native Swift apps with AI. When your app needs cloud storage or syncing, you can ask Bitrig to help configure CloudKit and connect it to your app’s data model. Learn more about CloudKit integration and Bitrig here .

title: Inside Amazon's first-ever drone delivery site in the UK
summary: The Prime Air site in Darlington, England is the first of its kind outside of the U.S.
body_text: Key takeaways Amazon drones are delivering parcels in Darlington, England, as part of the launch of Prime Air in the UK. It is the first time Prime Air is available to customers outside of the U.S. Customers within a 7.5-mile radius of the fulfillment center can have certain items delivered by drone. Just a few miles from the center of Darlington, England, is one of the country's most advanced Amazon fulfillment centers. The 465,000-square-foot site is fitted with state-of-the-art robotics technology and, as of February 2026, has been delivering parcels to customers by drone as part of the launch of Prime Air outside of the U.S. Amazon's fulfillment center in Darlington, England, serves as a hub for the company's drone delivery operations in the UK. Amazon first announced plans to launch its Prime Air drone delivery service in the UK in 2023, with the northern town of Darlington being confirmed as its first location in 2025 . It's the first time Amazon has expanded the service outside the U.S. "I'm proud that Darlington is the first Prime Air location outside the U.S., and that UK customers are now experiencing this." said Amazon UK Country Manager John Boumphrey. "The team has spent years making this safe, reliable, and real." How Amazon proved its new delivery drone is safe for takeoff Proving the safety of our new MK30 required creating—and acing—a battery of tests. Like in the U.S., deliveries in the UK are made within 60 minutes or less of a customer placing an order using the MK30 drone. The MK30 operates safely and highly autonomously using sophisticated, industry-leading detect-and-avoid technology, ensuring the safety of people, pets, and property. “The fact that a customer can now order an item and have it delivered by drone shows how we keep innovating for customers to make their lives easier,” said Boumphrey. “Not that long ago, two-day delivery felt incredible, and now we're using drones." How does Amazon's drone delivery work? Standing roughly five feet tall with a wingspan of about five and a half feet, the MK30 can carry packages weighing up to five pounds. Prime Air in the UK is currently available to customers with a garden, yard, or driveway in a 7.5-mile (12km) radius of the Darlington fulfillment center. When an item weighs 5lbs (2.2kg) or less and fits into a large shoebox, the customer can select the drone delivery option during checkout. Millions of items are currently eligible. During checkout, customers see a satellite map of their property showing options for "delivery zones," pre-identified using Amazon's digital mapping and AI systems. This is all done digitally—no physical survey of the property is needed. The customer can then select one of these drop-off zones and will be reminded to keep the area clear. How Amazon's delivery drones make smart landing decisions in unexpected conditions Prime Air’s advanced safety systems are built to safely land in the event of severe weather, unexpected events, and more to protect people, pets, and property. As soon as an order has been placed, things kick into action at the fulfillment center. The Darlington site is home to advanced robotics, meaning the customer's item is carried by Hercules , an autonomous lifting unit, to an associate who packs it in Prime Air packaging. Customized Prime Air boxes have cushioning technology at the bottom to protect the item during delivery. Safety is always our top priority. Our drone has received Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) approval to conduct operations, and an associate always carries out a pre-flight inspection of the drone. The associate ensures everything is in working order and installs a charged battery before loading the package into the underside of the aircraft. Sameer Mehmood, a ground handler at the site, explained: “One of the main things in the process is doing visual checks of the drone. I make sure the drone is in a good state, there's no damage, it's airworthy, and good to fly. You’ll see me checking the propellers, the struts, the motors, and doing a full 360 run of the drone." Each Prime Air package is secured in a compartment on the underside of the drone. An associate carries out a detailed inspection of the drone before takeoff. Before each flight, an associate installs a freshly charged battery, ensuring the drone has the power needed to complete its delivery and return to base. 01 / 04 Mehmood joined Amazon in 2020 as a part-time associate at the fulfillment center before becoming a team leader shortly after. In 2026, he received the training needed to join the Prime Air team. “I think it's a really cool job and career path to get into... It just amazes me every time that we're actually delivering packages by drone.” With inspections complete and the package loaded, the drone can take flight. It flies autonomously to the customer's property at speeds of up to 70mph and is quieter than an average delivery van. Once the drone has arrived at the customer's property, it begins its descent while identifying and steering clear of obstacles. Cameras are also monitoring the surrounding airspace and can navigate around unexpected aircraft. Once the package is loaded and pre-flight checks are complete, the drone is wheeled to the launchpad where it will begin its journey. The drone then drops the parcel from a safe height. Prime Air boxes have customized cushioning technology at the bottom to protect the item during delivery. Once the delivery is complete, the drone returns to the fulfillment center. Of course, British weather is famously unpredictable. The MK30 can fly safely in light rain and a range of temperatures and wind speeds, but if conditions make it unsafe to fly, Prime Air won't be available. Real-time weather signals are integrated into the checkout process, meaning that if conditions are unsuitable—heavy rain, high winds, or poor visibility—drone delivery simply won't appear as a shipping option, and the customer can choose another delivery method instead. Amazon’s newest UK delivery station aims to be the first to achieve new zero carbon certification outside the US The Stockton-on-Tees facility will use AI tracking, carbon-storing materials, and renewable energy to cut emissions by at least 20%. The technology behind the MK30 Engineers on the Prime Air team spent two years building the MK30 . Before a single customer package took flight in either the UK or U.S., the drone underwent more than 5,100 test flights—totaling over 900 hours in the air. Experts drew on safety protocols adapted from the aviation, automotive, and military industries, stress-testing the drone against everything from high winds to unexpected obstacles in its flight path. The MK30 underwent rigorous safety and engineering testing during development. The result is a machine built around one principle: no single point of failure should ever cause it to lose control. Every flight-critical system has a backup, and the drone's onboard perception system—a network of cameras and sensors—can detect and avoid obstacles that may not have been captured in satellite imagery. Sound was another priority. During flight and at the point of delivery, the MK30 is quieter than many common neighborhood and household noises. Our drones spend most of the flight at higher altitudes and sound heard on the ground is minimal and short-lived, typically lasting about 30 seconds. The level of sound during drop-off is quieter than an idling delivery truck parked curbside or a passing passenger car. During flight, at altitude the sound is comparable to an electric toothbrush or a window fan on low and typically can’t be heard indoors. The drone is a hexacopter design with six rotors, built for vertical take-off before transitioning to horizontal flight. For more news, visit About Amazon UK Amazon is guided by four principles: customer obsession rather than competitor focus, passion for invention, commitment to operational excellence, and long-term thinking. This is our story. How much does Amazon drone delivery cost? Currently in the UK, Prime Air delivery is included as part of an Amazon Prime membership with no additional delivery fee for members. As we extend the service to broader areas we will evaluate delivery fees consistent with other Amazon premium speed services. Next, find out how Amazon is using Japan’s iconic Shinkansen bullet trains to deliver packages . title: How to Get 40g of Protein in Every Meal
summary: In short Hitting 40g of protein per meal is the threshold for building lean muscle, but everyday food math makes it difficult. From weighing chicken breasts to navigating the high-calorie reality of plant proteins, here is exactly what it takes to reach your macro targets effortlessly. Table of contents What 40g of pro
body_text: What 40g of protein actually looks like on a plate For anyone focused on lean body mass, recovery, and metabolic performance, 40 grams of high-quality protein per meal is a critical operational threshold. Standard dietary guidelines often suggest smaller, spread-out portions, but rigorous systematic research demonstrates that higher per-meal protein doses drive superior muscle protein synthesis during resistance training. A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis by Nunes et al., published in the Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle, pooled randomized controlled trials in healthy adults and confirmed that increasing daily protein ingestion contributes to gains in lean body mass and muscle strength [1] . Hitting that 40g threshold in real life requires a significant shift in visual volume compared to typical dining out. Most standard restaurant bowls, salads, and casual entrees top out around 20 to 25 grams of protein, filling the rest of the plate with refined carbohydrates, heavy oils, and fillers. On a plate, 40 grams of complete protein translates to roughly 4.5 to 5.5 ounces of cooked lean meat, a substantial portion that visually dominates at least one-third to one-half of your dish. Meal Component Standard Restaurant Bowl 40g Protein Target Plate Protein Source Portion 2.5 to 3 oz cooked chicken (approx. 22g protein) 5 oz cooked skinless chicken breast (approx. 43g protein) Primary Calorie Source White rice, tortilla chips, heavy oil-based dressing Lean protein, fiber-rich vegetables, functional grains Total Protein Yield 20 to 25g 40 to 45g Satiety & Glucose Profile Rapid glucose spike, hunger returns in 2 to 3 hours Stable blood sugar, sustained fullness for 4 to 6 hours Protein math: Hitting 40g without doubling calories The primary challenge of hitting 40 grams of protein per meal is not simply eating more food; it is maximizing protein density while controlling overall caloric intake. Different whole-food protein sources carry drastically different calorie-to-protein ratios based on their inherent macronutrient makeup. According to official USDA FoodData Central reference values, cooked skinless chicken breast remains one of the most efficient whole-food protein anchors available, yielding 31.0 grams of complete protein per 100 grams at just 151 calories [2] . To hit 40 grams of protein from chicken breast, you need approximately 129 grams (4.5 ounces) of cooked meat, which costs under 195 calories. By contrast, achieving that same 40-gram protein floor using plant-based staples requires navigating a much higher caloric burden. Food Source Protein per 100g Portion Needed for 40g Protein Associated Calorie Cost Cooked Skinless Chicken Breast 31.0g 129g (4.5 oz) 195 kcal Atlantic Salmon Fillet 20.4g 196g (6.9 oz) 408 kcal Firm Calcium-Set Tofu 17.3g 231g (8.1 oz) 333 kcal Cooked Brown/Green Lentils 9.01g 444g (15.7 oz) 515 kcal As the numbers illustrate, using cooked lentils as your sole protein anchor demands nearly a full pound of food (444 grams) and over 500 calories just to reach 40 grams of protein, while simultaneously delivering over 35 grams of carbohydrate fiber. While legumes excel for gut health and micronutrients, relying on them as your exclusive protein source makes hitting strict macro targets in a calorie deficit mathematically difficult. Fish sits in between: salmon is less protein-dense per gram than skinless chicken breast, so a 40-gram serving means a noticeably larger fillet and a meaningfully higher calorie cost, because the fat comes along with the protein. Firm tofu offers a similar middle ground at 17.3 grams of protein per 100 grams, but still requires nearly double the total portion weight of lean poultry [4] . Why home cooking usually lands short When preparing meals at home, most people naturally default to recipes that yield between 25 and 30 grams of protein per serving. Commercial cookbooks and food blogs routinely prioritize fats, starches, and sweet glazes to maximize palatability, treating protein as a minor side element rather than the structural foundation of the meal. Furthermore, dietary assessment research is blunt about eyeballing portions: a systematic review of short-term self-report methods found that misestimating portion sizes is one of the largest contributors to measurement error, with both under- and overestimation showing up across most foods studied [6] . That is why unweighed protein servings and unrecorded cooking fats drift so far from what people believe they ate. Consistently hitting 40 grams of cooked protein through DIY prep creates several hidden operational friction points that wear down long-term adherence: Raw-to-cooked moisture loss: Poultry and beef lose weight in the pan, with typical yields of roughly 65 to 75 percent of raw weight, so 100 grams of raw chicken yields about 70 to 75 grams cooked, throwing off unweighed portion calculations [7] . Sauce and marinade calorie inflation: Commercial marinades and home dressings frequently add 150 to 300 unrecorded calories from seed oils and refined sugars without contributing a single gram of protein. Flavor fatigue and prep monotony: Cooking large batches of plain chicken breast leads to dry texture and rapid palate fatigue by day three of the weekly rotation. Time expenditure: Sourcing, trimming, weighing, cooking, and cleaning up after daily protein-dense meals consumes 7 to 10 hours per week. To overcome these barriers without spending every Sunday weighing raw poultry, smart eaters utilize structured frameworks like modular ingredient layering or turn to dedicated high-protein meal prep solutions that guarantee exact per-meal macros from the start. When delivery is simply faster For busy executives, founders, and active health optimizers across the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles, spending half a weekend prepping chicken breast is an inefficient use of time. We built Locale to eliminate every trade-off in clean, high-protein eating by enforcing a strict 40 to 60g protein floor across our entire menu . Instead of relying on dry, unseasoned meat or cheap fillers, we engineer macro density directly into every component using functional whole foods. We pack additional protein into our meals with bone broth-infused rice, edamame noodles, and rich Greek yogurt-based sauces. We source exclusively from named, trusted California producers, including Mary's Free Range Chicken, Creekstone Ranch, Rancho Gordo, and Lakeside Organic Farms. 40g to 60g protein floor: Every single meal hits your optimal macro target without requiring extra protein shakes or double portions. 8g+ fiber and zero seed oils: We cook strictly with organic extra-virgin olive oil and avocado oil, guaranteeing zero industrial seed oils or refined sugars. Third-party lab tested: We independently audit our food through Light Labs for heavy metals, pesticides, PFAS, and microplastics, publishing full test results publicly. Reusable glass packaging: Delivered fresh every Monday in microplastic-free, reusable glass jars that we pick up, sanitize, and reuse weekly. Our commitment to uncompromising quality is why tech leaders and health authors trust our kitchen to fuel their daily performance. As Connie Chan, General Partner at a16z, noted: 'After trying 5 meal services, I gave up on finding one that checked all my boxes, organic, no seed oils, no microplastics and still tasted good. But Locale nailed it.' Similar public endorsements from Max Lugavere (author of Genius Foods), Rahul (CEO of Superhuman), and Alex Mather (Co-Founder of The Athletic) reflect the compounding satisfaction our customers experience month after month. When compared against the combined cost of buying premium organic groceries, paying high-end restaurant prices for delivery, and losing 8 hours of executive work time to prep and cleanup, investing in pre-portioned, chef-crafted nutrition is the most cost-effective decision you can make. Explore our high-protein meal delivery menu today and subscribe to the Certified Clean High Protein Meal Subscription to put your daily macro targets on complete autopilot. Frequently asked questions How much chicken breast is needed for 40g of protein? Based on USDA data, 100g of chicken breast provides 31g of protein. To hit a 40g target, you need to eat roughly 130g (about 4.6 ounces) of cooked chicken breast per meal. Can you get 40g of protein from plant sources like lentils? Yes, but it requires a large volume of food. Cooked lentils provide 9g of protein per 100g, meaning you would need to consume nearly 450g of lentils to hit 40g, which significantly increases the total calorie count of the meal. Why is 40g of protein per meal recommended for active individuals? A 2022 meta-analysis by Nunes et al. demonstrates that higher daily protein ingestion supports the growth of lean body mass. Hitting 40g per meal ensures you maximize muscle synthesis and hit the high daily totals required by hard-training individuals. Why do standard home-cooked meals fall short of high protein targets? Most standard recipes balance macros for flavor, leaning heavily on fats and carbohydrates. Without strictly weighing your raw meats or protein sources, the average home-cooked dinner naturally lands around 25 to 30g of protein. Does Locale offer meals with 40g of protein? Yes. Locale is designed specifically for high-protein diets, with every prepared meal guaranteed to contain 40 to 60g of clean-ingredient protein to help you hit your daily macro targets effortlessly in the SF Bay Area and LA.
